title: Reading a pcap file
hints: Write one helper that reads a 32-bit value at an offset in either byte order, and decide the order once from the magic number. Every other field goes through that helper.

Before reading a record header, check that 16 bytes remain; before copying its data, check that `captured length` bytes remain. Compare by subtracting from the file size, so the check cannot overflow.
stretch: Open a real capture: save a few packets from Wireshark as "Wireshark/tcpdump - pcap", read the file into a vector with `std::ifstream` and print each record's time and length.
